editorial.copyrightPolicy: Publisher article text, review text, spec-sheet copy and press images are never copied; news is explained in Swoon'd's own words and linked. Photographers and photographs are discussed and described in words; the photographs themselves are not reproduced (spec section 40).

masteryModel.usefulCompetenceStatement: She can follow a conversation about light, exposure, lenses and gear, look at her photo and say something specific and kind about it, ask two good questions about how she got the shot, and say 'okay, I see why you love this' without bluffing.

licensingConstraints.constraint: Only original Swoon'd imagery (license original-swoond): procedural diagrams, vector illustrations, and in-house photographs with signed releases. Famous photographs are never reproduced; they are named, described in words and linked to the photographer's or a museum's page. Any later use of CC0 or public-domain museum images needs its own registered license id and per-asset provenance.
Shutter and film-advance sounds are original recordings or synthesised (original-swoond); no manufacturer sound libraries or video soundtracks.
Camera, lens, film and software brand names appear as text only (nominative use); no logos, product renders or manufacturer press images in lessons without written permission.
No embedded third-party video; deep-link to official channels.
Never copy review, news, spec-sheet or publisher text; paraphrase and link.

Sun, moon and twilight are computed on device. NOAA and NWS data are US-government public data; Open-Meteo needs a commercial plan for a paid app; NASA media usage guidelines apply to any NASA imagery (default: none used).
Photographers are named as facts and their work described; no likeness, fabricated quotes or implied endorsement. Learners are never encouraged to photograph a person without consent.

safetyConstraints: Never look at the sun through a camera, viewfinder or lens without a certified solar filter (ISO 12312-2 for eyewear; a purpose-made filter on the front of the lens); eclipse and sun content always carries this warning.

Landscape and outdoor scenarios follow conservative mainstream guidance: watch tides and surf, stay back from edges, do not shoot in lightning, tell someone your plan, and never trade safety for a shot. Scenarios are learning aids, not outdoor-safety training (see the hiking and camping courses).

Wildlife content puts the animal first: keep well back (National Park Service guidance is at least 100 yards from bears and wolves and 25 yards from other wildlife), never bait, call or flush animals, avoid nests and dens, no flash on nocturnal or nesting animals.

Portrait and street content is consent-first: ask, accept 'no', delete on request, take extra care with children, and never covertly photograph anyone, including the person the learner is trying to impress. Local law varies; Swoon'd states etiquette, not legal advice.

Film chemistry content stays at the level of 'labs exist and DIY development needs proper ventilation, gloves and eye protection from the chemical maker's instructions'; no unsupervised chemistry instructions.
Never encourage the learner to fake expertise, or to critique someone's work unkindly; the goal is genuine curiosity about why she loves photographing.
